changes.summary: New optional feature: you can claim a public address like yourname.servers.auoris.org for a Minecraft server on your own computer. If you do, a public DNS record points that name at your computer's current IP address, so anyone can look it up. Address names must follow the Acceptable Use Policy.
Clarified that a ban on a network stays in place even if the banned account is deleted (so deleting an account can't undo a ban), alongside the earlier note about the hashes we keep to enforce bans.

We now remember a one-way hash of the last few networks you sign in from, only to enforce bans (administrators can block a banned account's networks from creating new accounts, and server owners can block a banned member's networks from rejoining that server; nobody can see any address). A suspension also stops a Plus subscription from renewing, with no refund for the period already paid.
Added our support contact address (auoris-support@googlegroups.com) to the legal documents.
Deleting your account now cancels an active Plus subscription for you instead of blocking deletion; sign-up now checks your age (the date of birth is not stored).

Added server Sparks to the Subscription Terms; stated the age requirement more clearly (13, or 16 where the law says so); clarified what malware scanning does, what game presence reads, how long reports are kept, and added trademark notices.
First version of the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Acceptable Use Policy, Subscription and Gift Terms, and Copyright policy.
